claims.text: An origin is one of the three races of fae: inanimae, changelings and firstborn.
The firstborn are true fae who rose from the Mists of Creation long ago; new ones are born to firstborn or are sprites changed by strong cantrips.
Changelings are part fae, part human: made when a firstborn infant is swapped for a human one, which yields two changelings, or when humans stay long in fae realms and learn the Dominions.

Inanimae are fae of the natural world, usually springing from something tied to one of five elements: air, earth, fire, water or wood. They can breed with their own element, though most find the idea repulsive.

title: The Four Courts
summary: The seasonal factions of the fae.

claims.text: A Court is one of four seasonal factions; it shapes a fae's ideas, upbringing, magic and mien.

The Saining brings a fae into a Court in three steps: the Cleansing, three seasons living by the Court's ideals; the Naming, receiving a Courtly name; and the Acceptance, finishing training and formal entry.
Solstice fae, or Disgraced fae, never Sained, refused, were exiled, or had their Naming botched; they are scorned outcasts who find work as couriers and mercenaries.

title: The Oath-Truce
summary: The hundred-year peace between the Four Courts.

claims.text: The Oath-Truce is a pact among the Four Courts to halt hostilities for a hundred years.
It began in AD 1130 and so will end around 1230.

title: Agendas and the Patrons
summary: The political aims that cut across the Courts.

claims.text: An agenda is a fae's broad political or social aim. The common ones are Constantinian, Humanist, Militant and Truce-Bearer.
The Patrons count as an agenda but are really an organised faction, not a loose philosophy.
The Patrons want seasonal rule back: each Court ruling in its own season, then handing power on.

title: Dominions and Cantrips
summary: The four spheres of fae magic.

claims.text: A Dominion is one of four spheres of magic, each ruling a set of associations: Dawn, Day, Dusk and Night.
A cantrip is one specific magical use of a Dominion.
Unleashing lets Dominion magic loose without shaping it into a cantrip, steering it toward a hoped-for end; it is always obvious, and dangerous if it runs wild.

title: Weaving and the Mists
summary: The balance of order and chaos in fae magic.

claims.text: The Mists are the magical energy of Creation; fae use them both for magic and to hide from mortals.
Weaving is the force of order that lets fae channel Dominions into cantrips.
A fae whose Weaving grows too strong becomes Locked: unable to Unleash, and obsessed with order and routine.
A fae whose Mists grow too strong becomes Lost: unable to cast cantrips, and obsessed with chaos.
The mien is a fae's true faerie form, in which its Features show.
Lesser Features are only for looks; Greater Features also have effects in play.
A sprite is a minor fae spirit, usually bound to serve a stronger fae; one might be a cloud of butterflies, another a small blue flame. Sprites can grow into firstborn.
Fostering is the time before the Saining when a young fae learns fae society, history and the Dominions.
Every fae learns the Fostering tongue early, but most use it only when no Courtly language will serve.
An oathcircle is a band of fae bound by a shared purpose, whether war, exploring or company.
